questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to explore Southern Europe as I myself am from the Nothern part.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I am very happy I decided to go on exchange! Even though it was tough at times it was worth it in the end.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was difficult to find information about how to register for courses at the university. In addition, it was difficult to obtain the information we needed once we had finally arrived in Milan.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Once we arrived, the university staff were helpful, but much more laid-back than we were used to. It took us a little while to adjust and trust that all the practical matters would eventually fall into place.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They were very kind, but they handle the practical stuff way more laidback then what we are used to - therefore I would have preferred that they were more informative.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Finding accommodation was difficult. We spent a long time searching, and eventually, before arriving in Milan, we found an apartment on Airbnb. It was expensive, and when we arrived, we realized it was not suitable for me and the two fellow students from my home university that I was going to live with, as there were not enough bedrooms. We eventually found another apartment through
Idealista.com
. It was rented by a private landlord who was very kind, and the apartment was perfect for exchange students. In the end, everything worked out well, but finding the right place to live required a lot of time, effort, and energy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be expensive and challenging to find accommodation, but you can also get lucky. I also think it is easier to find a place once you have arrived, as you can visit apartments in person and make sure they are legitimate, reducing the risk of being scammed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Once we had arrived, everything was manageable. It was sometimes a bit complicated and unclear, but we felt confident that things would eventually work out. However, I think there was a lack of a single, comprehensive guide explaining everything that needed to be done, including the required registrations, paperwork, and documents to be signed.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to show up at the University. Afterwards you had to figure out yourself through the homepage on the computer which curses were in english.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There were someone at the office who could help explaining to process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Again, it was pretty laidback - At the beginning of the semester, you could explore and try out different courses. Once you had decided which ones to take, you simply had to email the course instructor, who would then register you on Ariel, the university's online learning platform.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Relax! But dont be afraid to email them with questions.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The selection of courses taught in English was limited. As a result, there was not a very wide selection of courses to choose from.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Due to the limited number of courses offered in English, I also enrolled in master's-level courses. The academic level was manageable and suited me okay. In addition, as I study European Ethnology, there were only a limited number of academically relevant courses available. For that reason, I chose master's-level courses to find options that were more suitable for my academic interests.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The atmosphere was more laid-back. Class attendance was lower, there were fewer breaks, and the overall environment was more relaxed.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- THE WESTERN TRADITION: MORAL AND POLITICAL VALUES
- INTELLECTUALS, POPULAR CULTURE, COLLECTIVE IDENTITIES:ITALY AND EUROPE IN THE 19TH AND 20TH CENTURIES
- BIOPOLITICS: BODIES, HEALTH AND FOOD

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The ones above!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Since we had to moved, it was an unexpected cost to pay deposit twice. 
We went to resturants alot, which was nice but obviously more espensive than eating at home.

But it is hard to put an estimate on all the things: Overall, I would say I spend more money on food (mainly because I ate out a lot) and housing compared to in my home country - but it is doable to make the exchange less expensive than I did!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery were more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't really join any.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I am unsure, as I didn't really go to any.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Eating at resturants and enyoing the weather.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to resturants, enjoy the parks, enjoy the weather.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was okay, again they are more laidback, so get use to that.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Their way of taking everything chill.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their way of taking everything chill - it was both good and bad.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Save up some money (or take a loan)
- Consider finding housing together with others
- DO IT!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Look at
Idealista.com
for housing, among others.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To be able to have lived for 6 months abroad.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Housing and feeling at home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
